title: Risk of Failing Liquidation Due to Blacklisted Recipient
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/logic/LiquidationLogic.sol#L39
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/logic/LiquidationLogic.sol#L99


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Within the [LiquidationLogic::liquidate()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/logic/LiquidationLogic.sol#L39) function, if `closeRatio < 1e18`, the remaining margin is transferred to a recipient specified by the vault owner on [L99](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/logic/LiquidationLogic.sol#L99). The recipient address is user-controlled and can be arbitrarily set using [PredyPool::updateRecipient()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/PredyPool.sol#L286). 

An issue arises when a vault, backed by `USDC` as collateral (one of the supported tokens), has its recipient set to a blacklisted address. This configuration causes partial liquidations to fail on [L99](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/logic/LiquidationLogic.sol#L99) because the `safeTransfer()` function reverts when attempting to transfer the remaining margin. Consequently, this allows vault owners to potentially prevent their vaults from being liquidated, leading to instances of accruing bad debt for the protocol when full liquidations cannot be executed.

## Proof of Concept
1. Alice creates a vault, sets the recipient to a blacklisted address, and uses `USDC` as collateral.
2. Due to price fluctuations, Alice's vault becomes liquidatable.
3. Bob attempts to liquidate Alice's vault by calling [BaseMarketUpgradeable::execLiquidationCall()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/base/BaseMarketUpgradable.sol#L96) with `closeRatio < 1e18`, resulting in the liquidation failing due to the `safeTransfer()` function reverting.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Two solutions can address this problem effectively:
1. Implement a pull-over-push pattern for the vault recipient, allowing recipients to claim funds rather than vaults pushing funds to recipients.
2. Modify the `LiquidationLogic::liquidate()` function to skip transactions involving blacklisted addresses, thereby enabling liquidations to proceed without encountering reverts.


## Assessed type

Token-Transfer

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/base/BaseMarket.sol#L13
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/base/BaseMarketUpgradable.sol#L25


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The difference in `BaseMarket.sol` and `BaseMarketUpgradable.sol` storage layout will cause data misalignment and state variable corruption.

## Proof of Concept

1. To inspect the storage slots in `BaseMarket.sol`
```
{
  "storage": [
    {
      "astId": 51975,
      "contract": "src/base/BaseMarket.sol:BaseMarket",
      "label": "whitelistFiller",
      "offset": 0,
      "slot": "1",
      "type": "t_address"
    },
    {
      "astId": 51982,
      "contract": "src/base/BaseMarket.sol:BaseMarket",
      "label": "_quoteTokenMap",
      "offset": 0,
      "slot": "2",
      "type": "t_mapping(t_uint256,t_address)"
    },
    {
      "astId": 51986,
      "contract": "src/base/BaseMarket.sol:BaseMarket",
      "label": "_whiteListedSettlements",
      "offset": 0,
      "slot": "3",
      "type": "t_mapping(t_address,t_bool)"
    }
  ]
}
```

2. To inspect the storage slots in `BaseMarketUpgradable.sol`

```
{
      "astId": 52295,
      "contract": "src/base/BaseMarketUpgradable.sol:BaseMarketUpgradable",
      "label": "whitelistFiller",
      "offset": 0,
      "slot": "1",
      "type": "t_address"
    },
    {
      "astId": 52298,
      "contract": "src/base/BaseMarketUpgradable.sol:BaseMarketUpgradable",
      "label": "_quoter",
      "offset": 0,
      "slot": "2",
      "type": "t_contract(PredyPoolQuoter)54168"
    },
    {
      "astId": 52302,
      "contract": "src/base/BaseMarketUpgradable.sol:BaseMarketUpgradable",
      "label": "_quoteTokenMap",
      "offset": 0,
      "slot": "3",
      "type": "t_mapping(t_uint256,t_address)"
    },
```

3. The inspections above show

Slot2:
BaseMarket has \_quoteTokenMap (a mapping) at slot 2.
BaseMarketUpgradable has \_quoter (a contract reference) at slot 2.

Slot3:
BaseMarket has \_whiteListedSettlements (a mapping) at slot 3.
BaseMarketUpgradable has \_quoteTokenMap (a mapping) at slot 3.

4. The cause is immutables are not stored in the storage. In `BaseMarket.sol:_quoter` is immutable, whereas `BaseMarketUpgradable.sol:_quoter` is not.

## Tools Used

Manual & Foundry

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Update BaseMarketUpgradable.sol

```diff
    address public whitelistFiller;

-    PredyPoolQuoter internal _quoter;
+    PredyPoolQuoter internal immutable _quoter;

    mapping(uint256 pairId => address quoteTokenAddress) internal _quoteTokenMap;

    mapping(address settlementContractAddress => bool) internal _whiteListedSettlements;
```


## Assessed type

Upgradable

title: The staleness of the quote token price is not checked
warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/2fb1e0ec7a52fc06c2e9c8e561bccba84302e4bb/src/PriceFeed.sol#L48-L51


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
An outdated price may be used to calculate the price of the quote token as the staleness is not checked in any way in the pricefeed. This would allow for arbitrage opportunities by any user.

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/2fb1e0ec7a52fc06c2e9c8e561bccba84302e4bb/src/PriceFeed.sol#L48-L51

The PriceFeed oracle within Predy makes use of both Chainlink and Pyth oracles in retrieving the price of a token pair. Usually, the chainlink oracle returns the price of the quotetoken while the base price is returned from the Pyth oracle.

```
function getSqrtPrice() external view returns (uint256 sqrtPrice) {
        //audit: Doesn't check staleness of quote price
        (, int256 quoteAnswer,,,) = AggregatorV3Interface(_quotePriceFeed).latestRoundData();

        
        IPyth.Price memory basePrice = IPyth(_pyth).getPriceNoOlderThan(_priceId, VALID_TIME_PERIOD);
.....................................................................

```
The basePrice returned from Pyth is checked for staleness during retrieval, however the price returned from Chainlink is not checked in any way for staleness. 
It is recommended even by Chainlink to always confirm the price returned from their oracles is not older than a given threshold and chainlink oracle prices may occasionally fall out date or become stale. What happens when a stale price is returned and is used to get the sqrtPrice is that arbitrage opportunities become possible.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
1. Check the `quoteAnswer` returned falls within a threshold ideally 1 - 24 hours.
```diff
  function getSqrtPrice() external view returns (uint256 sqrtPrice) {
       
-        (, int256 quoteAnswer,,,) = AggregatorV3Interface(_quotePriceFeed).latestRoundData();
+  (, int256 quoteAnswer,,uint256 updatedAt,) = AggregatorV3Interface(_quotePriceFeed).latestRoundData();
+ require(updatedAt <= MAX_THRESHOLD_PERIOD);

...........................................................
        
       
```


## Assessed type

Oracle

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L342-L344
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L342-L344


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the way `checkAutoHedgeAndClose` handles the case when `vault.openPosition.perp.amount` and `vault.openPosition.sqrtPerp.amount` are both zero.
[src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.solcheckAutoHedgeAndClose#L342-L344](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L342-L344)
```solidity
if (vault.openPosition.perp.amount == 0 && vault.openPosition.sqrtPerp.amount == 0) {
    return (false, false, positionId);
}
```
In this case, the function returns `false` for both `hedgeRequired` and `closeRequired`, and returns the original `positionId`. The code assumes that if the open position amounts are zero, there is no need for hedging or closing the position, but this assumption may not hold true in all cases.

Suppose a user has an open position with non-zero `perp.amount` and `sqrtPerp.amount`. Later, the position is closed or hedged, but the `userPosition` struct in the contract is not updated accordingly due to a bug or other issue.

In this case, when the `checkAutoHedgeAndClose function` is called, it will encounter the following condition: [src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.solcheckAutoHedgeAndClose#L342-L344](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L342-L344)
```solidity
if (vault.openPosition.perp.amount == 0 && vault.openPosition.sqrtPerp.amount == 0) {
    return (false, false, positionId);
}
```
Since the `vault.openPosition.perp.amount` and `vault.openPosition.sqrtPerp.amount` are both zero (due to the position being closed or hedged), the function will return `false` for both `hedgeRequired` and `closeRequired`, and return the original `positionId`.

However, this is an incorrect decision because the position has already been closed or hedged, and there may be other conditions or triggers (e.g., expiration time, price triggers) that require further action, such as settling the position or transferring funds.

## Tools Used
Vs

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Check the position's status/other relevant conditions before returning `false` for `hedgeRequired` and `closeRequired`. Alternatively, the function could return an additional status or error code to indicate that the position has already been closed or hedged, instead of assuming that no action is required.


## Assessed type

Error

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L408-L434


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The way `_getOrInitPosition` handles `positionId` parameter, the function allows creating a new position with an arbitrary `positionId` in a way that could lead to a collision with an existing position, resulting in unexpected behavior or data corruption.

Suppose there is an existing position with `positionId = 1` owned by trader1. An attacker can call `_getOrInitPosition` with `isCreatedNew = true`, `trader = attacker, pairId = someValidPairId, and positionId = 1`. The function will create a new position with `positionId = 1` for the attacker, overwriting the existing position owned by `trader1`. This can lead to data corruption and unexpected behavior, as the attacker's position will now be associated with trader1's position data.

## Proof of Concept
[src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#_getOrInitPosition](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L408-L434)

When `isCreatedNew` is `true`, the function creates a new `UserPosition` struct and assigns the provided `positionId`, trader, and `pairId` without any checks for uniqueness or collision with existing positions.

## Tools Used
Vs

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The function should ensure that the `positionId` is unique for each new position. Use a counter or a mapping to keep track of the next available `positionId` and assign it to the new position. Alternatively, the function could be modified to accept a `positionId` parameter only when `isCreatedNew` is `false` (i.e., when retrieving an existing position). For creating new positions, the function could generate a new unique `positionId` internally.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/perp/PerpMarketV1.sol#L282-L311
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/perp/PerpOrderV3.sol#L78-L80


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If the `PerpOrderV3Lib.resolve` does not properly validate the signature or allows an empty `bytes("") `as a valid signature, it could enable an attacker to execute orders without proper authorization. 

_An attacker could potentially execute unauthorized trades, leading to the loss of funds held in user positions or the contract itself._

[src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#quoteExecuteOrderV3#L282-L311](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/perp/PerpMarketV1.sol#L282-L311)
```solidity
    // ...
    _predyPool.trade(
        IPredyPool.TradeParams(
            perpOrder.pairId,
            userPosition.vaultId,
            tradeAmount,
            0,
            abi.encode(
                CallbackData(
                    CallbackSource.QUOTE3,
                    perpOrder.info.trader,
                    0,
                    perpOrder.leverage,
                    PerpOrderV3Lib.resolve(perpOrder, bytes("")), // <-- Potential vulnerability
                    0
                )
            )
        ),
        _getSettlementDataFromV3(settlementParams, filler)
    );
}
```
[src/markets/perp/PerpOrderV3.sol#resolve](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/markets/perp/PerpOrderV3.sol#L78-L80)
```solidity
function resolve(PerpOrderV3 memory perpOrder, bytes memory sig) internal pure returns (ResolvedOrder memory) {
    return ResolvedOrder(perpOrder.info, perpOrder.entryTokenAddress, perpOrder.marginAmount, hash(perpOrder), sig);
}
```
In the `quoteExecuteOrderV3`, `PerpOrderV3Lib.resolve` is called with an empty `bytes("")` as the signature. The resolve function does not properly validate the signature or allow an empty `bytes("")` as a valid signature.

## Proof of Concept
Assume that the `resolve` does not validate the signature and returns a `ResolvedOrder` struct with the provided signature, even if it's an empty `bytes("")`. In this case, an attacker could call the `quoteExecuteOrderV3` with a crafted `PerpOrderV3` struct and an empty `bytes("")` as the signature, which would bypass any signature verification and allow the attacker to execute unauthorized trades.

```solidity
// Attacker's code
PerpOrderV3 maliciousOrder = PerpOrderV3(
    // Crafted order details
    ...
);

// Call quoteExecuteOrderV3 with an empty signature
perpMarket.quoteExecuteOrderV3(maliciousOrder, SettlementParamsV3(...), attacker);
```
If the `resolve` function does not properly validate the signature, the `quoteExecuteOrderV3` would execute the trade based on the attacker's crafted `PerpOrderV3` struct.

## Tools Used
Vs

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The `PerpOrderV3Lib.resolve` function should be reviewed and updated to ensure that it properly validates the provided signature. It should not allow an empty `bytes("")` as a valid signature unless explicitly intended. Additionally, the `quoteExecuteOrderV3` function should be updated to obtain the signature from a trusted source (e.g., a signed order struct) before calling `PerpOrderV3Lib.resolve`.


## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/PredyPool.sol#L187
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/PredyPool.sol#L177


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The protocol team expects that anyone can freely add pairs to the PredyPool. Currently, adding a new pair requires the user to have an operator role. Given that everyone will be able to add pairs, the operator role can be assigned to everyone or removed entirely.

The `withdrawProtocolRevenue` function, which handles the logic for withdrawing the protocol revenue, has an `onlyOperator` restriction. If anyone can have the operator role or it is removed entirely, then everyone can withdraw the protocol revenue because the tokens are sent directly to` msg.sender`.

```solidity
if (amount > 0) {
    ERC20(pool.token).safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount);
}
```

The funds of the protocol can easily be drained if the operator role is not handled correctly, especially if everyone can have the role.


## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Send the revenue to the treasury address of the protocol instead of to msg.sender


## Assessed type

Access Control

# Vulnerability details

## Summary

When utilizing Chainlink in L2 chains like Arbitrum, it's important to ensure that the prices provided are not falsely perceived as fresh, even when the sequencer is down. This vulnerability could potentially be exploited by malicious actors to gain an unfair advantage.

## Vulnerability Detail

If the Arbitrum Sequencer goes down, oracle data will not be kept up to date, and thus could become stale. 
You can review Chainlink docs on [L2 Sequencer Uptime Feeds](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds)  for more details on this.

As a result, users may be able to use the protocol while oracle feeds are stale. This could cause many problems, but as a simple example:

- A user has an account with 100 tokens, valued at 1 ETH each, and no borrows
- The Arbitrum sequencer goes down temporarily
- While it's down, the price of the token falls to 0.5 ETH each
- The current value of the user's account is 50 ETH, so they should be able to borrow a maximum of 200 ETH to keep account healthy ((200 + 50) / 200 = 1.2)
- Because of the stale price, the protocol lets them borrow 400 ETH ((400 + 100) / 400 = 1.2)

## Impact

If the Arbitrum sequencer goes down, the protocol will allow users to continue to operate at the previous (stale) rates.


## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

code example of Chainlink:
https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/l2-sequencer-feeds#example-code


## Assessed type

# Vulnerability details

## Summary

Chainlink's latestRoundData() is used but there is no check if the return value indicates stale data. This could lead to stale prices according to the Chainlink documentation:
- https://docs.chain.link/docs/historical-price-data/#historical-rounds

## Vulnerability Detail

The `getSqrtPrice` function uses Chainlink's latestRoundData() to get the latest price. However, there is no check if the return value indicates stale data.

```

function getSqrtPrice() external view returns (uint256 sqrtPrice) {
        (, int256 quoteAnswer,,,) = AggregatorV3Interface(_quotePriceFeed).latestRoundData(); //@audit

        IPyth.Price memory basePrice = IPyth(_pyth).getPriceNoOlderThan(_priceId, VALID_TIME_PERIOD);

        require(basePrice.expo == -8, "INVALID_EXP");

        require(quoteAnswer > 0 && basePrice.price > 0);

        uint256 price = uint256(int256(basePrice.price)) * Constants.Q96 / uint256(quoteAnswer);
        price = price * Constants.Q96 / _decimalsDiff;

        sqrtPrice = FixedPointMathLib.sqrt(price);
    }

```

## Impact

Old prices mean traders will get wrong PnL values for their positions, leading to liquidations or getting more/less than they should,

## Tools Used.

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Add a staleness threshold number of seconds configuration parameter, and ensure that the price fetched is within that time range

Oracle

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The 'updateFeeRatio' function does not validate the input 'feeRatio' before passing it to 'AddPairLogic.updateFeeRatio'. This could lead to an exploitable situation where an attacker can set an high fee ratio that could potentially clause too high FreeRation

## Proof of Concept

File: contracts/code4rena/2024-05-predy/src/PredyPool.sol
147:     function updateFeeRatio(uint256 pairId, uint8 feeRatio) external onlyPoolOwner(pairId) {
148:         AddPairLogic.updateFeeRatio(globalData.pairs[pairId], feeRatio);
149:     }


1. **Identify the Target Pair**: The attacker identifies a pair in the system where they have significant holdings or influence.

2. **Call `updateFeeRatio` with an Extreme Value**: The attacker calls the `updateFeeRatio` function with a `pairId` corresponding to the identified pair and a `feeRatio` set to the maximum value (255).

3. **Impact on Trading Fees**: Since the fee ratio is set to an extremely high value, any token swaps involving this pair will incur a disproportionately high fee. This high fee can disrupt normal trading activities and discourage users from trading in this pair.

4. **Manipulation of Market Dynamics**: The attacker can manipulate the market dynamics by strategically using this high fee to their advantage. For instance, they can buy or sell tokens at a lower volume, knowing that the high fees will deter others from entering the market, thus allowing the attacker to control the price movements.

5. **Economic Impact**: The economic impact of this manipulation can be significant. The attacker can potentially profit from price discrepancies caused by the high fees, while other users might suffer losses due to the inability to trade efficiently.


## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps

To correct this vulnerability, the following changes should be implemented:

- **Limit the Range of Fee Ratio**: Modify the `updateFeeRatio` function to accept a `feeRatio` that is within a reasonable range. For example, you could limit the `feeRatio` to a maximum of 10 by using a custom error or a conditional check before updating the fee ratio or use validateFeeRatio at
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/logic/AddPairLogic.sol#L205-L207

function updateFeeRatio(uint256 pairId, uint8 feeRatio) external onlyPoolOwner(pairId) {
    require(feeRatio <= 20, "Fee ratio too high"); 
    AddPairLogic.updateFeeRatio(globalData.pairs[pairId], feeRatio);
}
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/e96f378007e3dc56b184079f0c0e4fe48a72efaa/src/libraries/logic/LiquidationLogic.sol#L39


# Vulnerability details

## Description 
The liquidate function in the LiquidationLogic library is responsible for executing the liquidation process. It involves several critical steps, including updating interest growth, checking if the vault is in danger, executing trades, updating the vault's margin, and transferring any remaining margin.

However, the function does not account for the possibility of flash deposits, where a liquidator could temporarily deposit a large amount of assets to manipulate the vault's margin or value within a single transaction. This manipulation can lead to incorrect liquidation decisions, allowing the liquidator to earn extra yield unfairly.
 

## Impact
1. The manipulated values can lead to incorrect liquidation decisions, either preventing necessary liquidations or triggering unnecessary ones.

2. The liquidator can earn extra yield by exploiting the temporary inflated values.

## Proof of Concept
Scenario: 
- A liquidator deposits a large amount of assets into the vault within a single transaction.
- The temporary deposit inflates the vault's margin or value, making it appear safer or more liquidatable.
- The liquidator triggers the liquidation process based on the manipulated values.
- After the liquidation, the liquidator withdraws the deposited assets within the same transaction.

## Tools Used
manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

1. Time-Weighted Averages:
- Implement time-weighted average values for margin and vault value calculations to mitigate the impact of temporary deposits.
- This approach ensures that the calculations are based on more stable and representative values rather than temporary spikes.

2. Deposit Lock Periods:
- Introduce a lock period for deposits to prevent immediate withdrawals within the same transaction.
- This strategy ensures that any deposited assets remain in the vault for a minimum duration, reducing the potential for flash deposit exploits.

3. Flash Loan Detection:
- Implement mechanisms to detect and prevent flash loan attacks by monitoring large, sudden deposits and withdrawals within a single transaction.
- This can involve setting thresholds for maximum allowed deposits or withdrawals within a single transaction and flagging suspicious activity.



## Assessed type

# Vulnerability details

## Description 
The trade function in the PredyPool contract can be called without ensuring that initial states and setup processes are correctly executed. This includes pair registration, risk parameter setup, price oracle configuration, collateral and margin management, allowlist configuration, and fee setup. Bypassing these initial states can lead to significant issues, including financial instability, incorrect trade execution, protocol exploitation, and revenue loss.
```
function trade(TradeParams memory tradeParams, bytes memory settlementData) external nonReentrant returns (TradeResult memory tradeResult) {
    globalData.validate(tradeParams.pairId);

    if (globalData.pairs[tradeParams.pairId].allowlistEnabled && !allowedTraders[msg.sender][tradeParams.pairId]) {
        revert TraderNotAllowed();
    }

    tradeParams.vaultId = globalData.createOrGetVault(tradeParams.vaultId, tradeParams.pairId);

    return TradeLogic.trade(globalData, tradeParams, settlementData);
}
```

## Impact
1. Financial Instability:
- Incorrect trade execution, insufficient collateral, and mismanaged risk parameters can lead to financial instability, increasing the risk of defaults and liquidation issues.

2. Incorrect Trade Execution:
- Operating on invalid or non-existent pairId values, incorrect asset pricing, and unauthorized trading can result in trades being executed under unfavorable or unintended conditions, leading to financial losses.

3. Protocol Exploitation:
- Unauthorized traders exploiting the protocol due to unconfigured allowlists can lead to misuse and potential security vulnerabilities.

4. Revenue Loss:
- Incorrect fee collection can impact the protocol's revenue, affecting its financial sustainability and ability to cover operational costs.

## Proof of Concept
Scenario:
- A user calls the trade function without prior initialization and setup of pairs, risk parameters, price oracles, collateral, allowlists, and fees.

Steps: 
- The trade function is called with a pairId that has not been registered.
- The function attempts to validate the pairId, create or retrieve a vault, and execute the trade logic.
- Due to the lack of initial setup, the function operates on uninitialized or incorrect data, leading to unexpected behavior and potential financial losses.

Impact:
- The protocol's state could be corrupted, leading to financial losses or operational failures.
- Unauthorized trades could be executed, compromising the integrity and safety of the protocol.
- Incorrect fee collection could impact the protocol's revenue and financial sustainability.

## Tools Used
Manual review

1. Add checks to ensure that the initialize function has been called before allowing any trades.

2. Ensure that the pairId is valid and registered before executing trades.

3. Add checks to ensure that risk parameters and price oracles are configured before allowing trades.

4. Add checks to ensure that collateral and margin requirements are configured before allowing trades.

5. Add checks to ensure that fees are configured before allowing trades. This ensures that the protocol collects the intended revenue from each trade.

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/PredyPool.sol#L337


# Vulnerability details

## Description 
The createVault function in the PredyPool contract relies on the globalData.validate(pairId) function to ensure the pairId is valid. However, the function references globalData.createOrGetVault(0, pairId), which does not exist in the provided code. This absence results in incomplete functionality, leading to potential errors, state inconsistencies, and a poor user experience.

```
function createVault(uint256 pairId) external returns (uint256) {
    globalData.validate(pairId);
    return globalData.createOrGetVault(0, pairId); // This function does not exist
}
```

## Impact
1. The createVault function cannot create or retrieve a vault without a defined mechanism, resulting in incomplete functionality.

2. Interacting with an undefined function could lead to state inconsistencies or unexpected behavior in the contract.

3. An incomplete function could be exploited by malicious actors to cause unintended behavior or disrupt the protocol's operations.

## Proof of Concept
Scenario:
- A user attempts to create a vault using the createVault function.

Steps: 
- The user calls createVault with a valid pairId.
- The function calls globalData.validate(pairId) to ensure the pairId is valid.
- The function then attempts to call globalData.createOrGetVault(0, pairId), which does not exist.
- The function fails to execute properly, resulting in a revert or error.

## Tools Used
Manual review 

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
1. Implement a function to create or retrieve a vault, ensuring that the createVault function can perform its intended operation. This function should handle the creation of a new vault if the vaultId is zero or retrieve an existing vault if the vaultId is provided.

2. Ensure that the createVault function includes all necessary validations, such as:
- Checking for existing vaults to prevent duplicates.
- Validating caller permissions to ensure only authorized users can create vaults.
- Ensuring that the protocol is not paused or undergoing maintenance.
- Validating that all necessary parameters (risk parameters, interest rate models, price oracles) are set for the pairId.
- Checking that the caller meets the initial collateral requirements.
- Ensuring that the creation of new vaults does not exceed predefined limits.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Users face potential unjust liquidation due to fillers having access to two different prices in a single transaction.
This issue may also stem from user oversight, as traders must grasp and mitigate the associated risks.
## Proof of Concept
When a trade is initiated, the trader signs the order and forwards both the order and signature to a filler. The filler then calls either executeOrderV3 or executeTrade(). However, the system does not ensure that prices from Pyth are updated before being used in trade execution. This vulnerability enables a filler to manipulate execution by using outdated prices, potentially leading to user liquidation.

The Pyth oracles allow for retrieving two distinct prices within one transaction, which can be exploited for arbitrage. Pyth network prices update every 400ms, indicating that the latest price recorded on-chain may not be the most recent one.

## Tool Used
Manual review

## Recommended  Mitigation Steps 
To mitigate risks associated with significant discrepancies, ensure that all Pyth pricing data used during trade execution is updated by calling Pyth's updatePriceFeeds() function to obtain the latest prices.

# Vulnerability details


## Impact: 
This is a popular bug Case: where if a protocol were to allow  users to borrow their LTV exactly they might be liquidated in the next block.

In cases where a protocol allows users to borrow their exact Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio, there is a risk of immediate liquidation in the following block. Currently, in Predy, this scenario seems feasible, leading to potential unfair liquidation, financial losses, and diminished trust in the protocol.


## Proof of Concept:
The protocol's liquidation logic permits borrowing conditions where the user's liquidatable state matches their liquidation threshold, resulting in potential immediate liquidation.

Similar issues have been documented in the past, such as in this code4rena report:
- https://github.com/code-423n4/2023-02-sturdy-findings/issues/16

## Tool Used: 
Manual Review.
## Recommended Mitigation Steps: 
Incorporate a buffer to the liquidation threshold, ensuring users have a safety margin and reducing the risk of immediate liquidation in the subsequent block.

Adding this buffer will provide a safety net, preventing immediate liquidation due to minor fluctuations in collateral value.

Other

Currently, withdrawals are queued in an array and processed sequentially in a for loop. However, a safeTransfer() to USDC blacklisted user will fail. It will also brick the withdrawal system because the blacklisted user is never cleared.

See [Tokens with Blocklists](https://github.com/d-xo/weird-erc20?tab=readme-ov-file#tokens-with-blocklists)

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

consider Implementing 2-step withdrawals: - In a for loop, increase the user's amount that can be safely withdrawn. - A user himself withdraws his balance

`callUniswapObserve()`is used to get TWAP price tick using uniswap oracle. if `int24(tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0])` is negative and `((tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0]) % secondsAgo != 0,` the value returned will be higher than it should be, which affects the protocol from getting accurate prices and opens possibility for some price manipulations and arbitrage opportunities.

https://vscode.dev/github/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/UniHelper.sol#L35-L75

The tick should be rounded down as it's done in the [uniswap library](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-periphery/blob/main/contracts/libraries/OracleLibrary.sol#L36)

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider handling rounding for negative tick values.

`if (tickCumulativesDelta < 0 && (tickCumulativesDelta % secondsAgo != 0)) arithmeticMeanTick--;`

Uniswap

# Lines of code

https://vscode.dev/github/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/settlements/UniswapSettlement.sol#L22-L56


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

If a user attempts to swap ETH using `swapExactIn` or `swapExactOut`, the transaction will fail. Because the functions currently handle ERC20 tokens only and do not account for ETH, Users who want to be paid out in ETH or WETH will be forced to probably have the Swapper not function properly for a key pair or pay bots to perform useless actions.

## Proof of Concept

https://vscode.dev/github/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/settlements/UniswapSettlement.sol#L22-L56

If a user calls `swapExactIn` with ETH as the input asset, The function tries to execute `ERC20(baseToken).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountIn)` and since ETH is not an ERC20 token, the transaction will revert.

The `UniswapSettlement.sol` contract returns a quote per pair of tokens. However, since Uniswap pools only consist of WETH (not ETH) and are ordered by token address, it performs two conversions first: _convert() converts ETH to WETH for both base and quote tokens, and _sort() orders the pairs by token address.

The assumption is that this will be set to a moderate amount (approximately 5%) to incentivize bots to perform the swaps, but will be overridden with a value of ~0% for the same tokens, to ensure that bots aren't paid for swaps they don't need to perform.

The problem is that these overrides are set on the scqp (sorted, converted tokens), not the actual token addresses. For this reason, ETH and WETH are considered identical in terms of overrides.

Therefore, Swapper owners who want to be paid out in ETH (ie where $tokenToBeneficiary = ETH) have two options:

They can set the WETH-WETH override to 0%, which successfully stops bots from earning a fee on ETH-ETH trades, but will not provide any incentive for bots to swap WETH in the swapper into ETH. This makes the Swapper useless for WETH.

They can keep the WETH-WETH pair at the original ~5%, which will incentivize WETH-ETH swaps, but will also pay 5% to bots for doing nothing when they take ETH out of the contract and return ETH. This makes the Swapper waste user funds.

The same issues exist going in the other direction, when $tokenToBeneficiary = WETH.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Consider modifying the `swapExactIn` and `swapExactOut` functions parameters to accommodate ETH transactions by adding `payable`.


## Assessed type

Uniswap

```

Manual Review, Josephdara

Set a max threshold for ``updateAt``. If `block.timestamp - updateAt` exceeds that threshold, revert the transaction
Also, fetch the minAnswer and revert if price has hit that value.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/libraries/UniHelper.sol#L56-L73


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
The function `callUniswapObserve` is used to get twap price tick using `IUniswapV3PoolOracle.observe.selector` which is then used to calculate the `int24 tick`.

The problem is that in case if `(tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0])` is negative, the tick should be rounded down as it's done in the `OracleLibrary` from uniswap.

As result, in case if `(tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0])`is negative and `(tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0]) % secondsAgo != 0`, then returned tick will be bigger then it should be, hence incorrect prices would be used.

## Proof of Concept
`Unihelper:::callUniswapObserve()`:
```solidity
        int56[] memory tickCumulatives = abi.decode(data, (int56[]));

        int24 tick = int24((tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0]) / int56(int256(ago)));

        uint160 sqrtPriceX96 = TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(tick);

```

In Uniswap's `OracleLibrary:::consult()`:

```solidity
        int56 tickCumulativesDelta = tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0];
        uint160 secondsPerLiquidityCumulativesDelta =
            secondsPerLiquidityCumulativeX128s[1] - secondsPerLiquidityCumulativeX128s[0];

        arithmeticMeanTick = int24(tickCumulativesDelta / secondsAgo);
        // Always round to negative infinity
        if (tickCumulativesDelta < 0 && (tickCumulativesDelta % secondsAgo != 0)) arithmeticMeanTick--;
```
## Tools Used

Manual Review, Solodit, Josephdara, https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-periphery/blob/697c2474757ea89fec12a4e6db16a574fe259610/contracts/libraries/OracleLibrary.sol#L16-L41

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Round down the `int24 tick`: 
```solidity
if (tickCumulativesDelta < 0 && (tickCumulativesDelta % secondsAgo != 0)) tick--;
```


## Assessed type

Math

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In Trade.sol, the function trade() in order to get tradeResult.sqrtPrice it calls getSqrtPrice() that calls UniHelper.convertSqrtPrice() that use ```IUniswapV3Pool(uniswapPoolAddress).slot0()``` to get the value of sqrtPriceX96, which is used to perform the swap if ```if (totalBaseAmount == 0)```. However, the sqrtPriceX96 is pulled from Uniswap.slot0, which is the most recent data point and can be manipulated easily via MEV bots and Flashloans with sandwich attacks. This can cause loss of funds when interacting with the swap function.

## Proof of Concept

The problem is that in case if tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0] is negative, then timeWeightedTick should be rounded down like [Uniswap library](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-periphery/blob/main/contracts/libraries/OracleLibrary.sol#L36)

As result, in case of tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0] is negative and (tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0]) % ago != 0, tick will be bigger then it should be. Which opens possibility for arbitrage opportunities.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Tick should be rounded down in this case:
```solidity
    int24 tick = int24((tickCumulatives[0] - tickCumulatives[1]) / int56(uint56(ago)));
 +  if ((tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0]) < 0 && ((tickCumulatives[1] - tickCumulatives[0]) % ago != 0)) tick--;
```


## Assessed type

Uniswap

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/a9246db5f874a91fb71c296aac6a66902289306a/src/PriceFeed.sol#L54-L55


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the `PriceFeed` contract, the calculation of `price` by the `getSqrtPrice` function involves a division before a multiplication, which can lead to precision loss.

Given that the purpose of this function is to provide an accurate square root price of the base token quoted in the quote token, maintaining precision is crucial.

## Proof of Concept
In the calculation of `price`, `basePrice.price` is converted to `int256` and then `uint256`, multiplied by `Constants.Q96`, and then divided by `uint256(quoteAnswer)` to calculate an initial `price` value. Subsequently, this `price` is multiplied by `Constants.Q96` again and divided by `_decimalsDiff`.

The sequence of these operations means that the division by `uint256(quoteAnswer)` in the first line occurs before the multiplication by `Constants.Q96` in the second line, potentially leading to a loss of precision.

```solidity
        uint256 price = uint256(int256(basePrice.price)) * Constants.Q96 / uint256(quoteAnswer);
        price = price * Constants.Q96 / _decimalsDiff;
```

Precision loss in the price calculation can lead to inaccurate pricing, which might affect the reliability of the `getSqrtPrice` function.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To ensure that precision is maintained, reorder the operations to perform multiplication before division to minimize intermediate rounding.

```solidity
uint256 price = (uint256(int256(basePrice.price)) * Constants.Q96 * Constants.Q96) / (uint256(quoteAnswer) * _decimalsDiff);
```

This approach ensures that multiplications are done first, minimizing the impact of division truncation. By multiplying the numerators together before dividing by the product of the denominators (`quoteAnswer` and `_decimalsDiff`), you reduce the chance of losing precision.







## Assessed type

Other

The contract should implement a check to verify whether the recipient address is blacklisted before attempting the `safeTransfer`. 

If the recipient is blacklisted, the contract could redirect the funds to a predefined backup address.

This ensures that the liquidation process can proceed smoothly despite the blacklisted status of the `vault.recipient`.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/PriceFeed.sol#L46


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The absence of a round completeness check can result in stale prices and incorrect price returns, potentially causing financial losses. 
The getOraclePrice() function in the oracle wrapper relies on the latestRoundData() call to fetch the price of a specific token. While the returned timestamp is validated, the round completeness is not. 
As per Chainlink's documentation, this function does not produce an error if no answer is reached but instead returns 0 or outdated data. Consequently, the external Chainlink oracle, which supplies index price information, poses a risk due to its reliance on third-party data sources.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/PriceFeed.sol#L46


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Chainlink aggregators have a built in circuit breaker if the price of an asset goes outside of a predetermined price band. The result is that if an asset expirences a huge drop in value (i.e. LUNA crash) the price of the oracle will continue to return the minPrice instead of the actual price of the asset. This would allow user to continue borrowing with the asset but at the wrong price. This is exactly what happened to Venus on BSC when LUNA imploded.

ChainlinkFeedRegistry#latestRoundData pulls the associated aggregator and requests round data from it. ChainlinkAggregators have minPrice and maxPrice circuit breakers built into them. This means that if the price of the asset drops below the minPrice, the protocol will continue to value the token at minPrice instead of it's actual value. This will allow users to take out huge amounts of bad debt and bankrupt the protocol.

Example: TokenA has a minPrice of $1. The price of TokenA drops to $0.10. The aggregator still returns $1 allowing the user to borrow against TokenA as if it is $1 which is 10x it's actual value.

Note: Chainlink oracles are used a just one piece of the OracleAggregator system and it is assumed that using a combination of other oracles, a scenario like this can be avoided. However this is not the case because the other oracles also have their flaws that can still allow this to be exploited. As an example if the chainlink oracle is being used with a UniswapV3Oracle which uses a long TWAP then this will be exploitable when the TWAP is near the minPrice on the way down. In a scenario like that it wouldn't matter what the third oracle was because it would be bypassed with the two matching oracles prices. If secondary oracles like Band are used a malicious user could DDOS relayers to prevent update pricing. Once the price becomes stale the chainlink oracle would be the only oracle left and it's price would be used.

In the event that an asset crashes (i.e. LUNA) the protocol can be manipulated to give out loans at an inflated price

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If the Arbitrum Sequencer goes down, oracle data will not be kept up to date, and thus could become stale. However, users are able to continue to interact with the protocol directly through the contract. You can review Chainlink docs on L2 Sequencer Uptime Feeds for more details on this.
As a result, users may be able to use the protocol while oracle feeds are stale. This could cause many problems, but as a simple example:

A user has an account with 100 tokens, valued at 1 ETH each, and no borrows
The Arbitrum sequencer goes down temporarily
While it's down, the price of the token falls to 0.5 ETH each
The current value of the user's account is 50 ETH, so they should be able to borrow a maximum of 200 ETH to keep account healthy ((200 + 50) / 200 = 1.2)
Because of the stale price, the protocol lets them borrow 400 ETH ((400 + 100) / 400 = 1.2)

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/tree/main/src/PredyPool.sol#L68
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/tree/main/src/markets/gamma/GammaTradeMarket.sol#L67
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/tree/main/src/markets/perp/PerpMarketV1.sol#L90


# Vulnerability details

## Summary

`PredyPool`, `GammaTradeMarket`, `PerpMarketV1` contract uses upgradable contracts. 
Calling the `initialize()` function directly on the implementation contract behind a proxy is dangerous. 
In such case, if the implementation calls self-destruct or performs delegate calls it’s possible to delete the implementation leaving the contract bricked. 

## Vulnerability Detail

Upgradable contracts are an essential protocol feature, allowing for flexible updates and maintenance. 
Contracts should include a default constructor calling `_disableInitializers()` function: 
(https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable/blob/master/contracts/proxy/utils/Initializable.sol#L192) of `Initializable.sol`.

## Impact

When implementing upgradable contracts, ensuring that the `initialize()` function is not accidentally called directly on the implementation contract behind the proxy is crucial. 

If this occurs and the implementation contract contains self-destruct or delegate calls, it can result in the unintended deletion of the implementation contract.

## Tool used

Manual Review

## Recommendation

1. Please update PredyPool#`constructor()` as follows.

```diff
contract PredyPool is 
	IPredyPool, IUniswapV3MintCallback, Initializable, ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable {
	...
	
	constructor() {
++		_disableInitializers();
	}
	
	...
}
```

2. Please update GammaTradeMarket#`constructor()` as follows.

```diff
contract GammaTradeMarket is 
	IFillerMarket, BaseMarketUpgradable, ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable {
	...
	
	constructor() {
++		_disableInitializers();
	}
	
	...
}
```

3. Please update PerpMarketV1#`constructor()` as follows.

```diff
contract PerpMarketV1 is BaseMarketUpgradable, ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable {
	...
	
	constructor() {
++		_disableInitializers();
	}
	
	...
}
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/ScaledAsset.sol#L200-L207
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/ScaledAsset.sol#L235-L241


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
If `getTotalDebtValue(tokenState)` > `getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)` is not considered, the ratio may be greater than 1, so the supply interest rate will be amplified, causing the economic system to face the risk of instability. By limiting the ratio to 1, the supply interest rate is ensured to be within a reasonable range and the stability of the system is maintained.
## Proof of Concept
According to the design of the protocol, the calculation method of utilization needs to consider the ratio of `getTotalDebtValue(tokenState)/getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)`.
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/ScaledAsset.sol#L235-L241
```sol
        uint256 utilization = FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(
            getTotalDebtValue(tokenState), Constants.ONE, getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)
        );

        if (utilization > 1e18) {
            return 1e18;
        }
```
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/ScaledAsset.sol#L200
Because the supply interest rate is `InterestRate * Utilization * (1 - ReserveFactor)`, and the calculation of the Utilization value must take into account the situation where `getTotalDebtValue(tokenState)`>`getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)` (1 without scaling, 1e18 with scaling)

```sol
        // supply interest rate is InterestRate * Utilization * (1 - ReserveFactor)
        uint256 supplyInterestRate = FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(
            FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(
                _interestRate, getTotalDebtValue(tokenState), getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)
            ),
            100 - _reserveFactor,
            100
        );
```
We can see that there is no scaling of 1e18 in this calculation, so we only need to consider getTotalDebtValue(tokenState)/getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)>1

### Prove that in this case, supplyInterestRate will be very large and has no upper limit:

`_interestRate`：1e16
`getTotalDebtValue(tokenState)`：10e18
`getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)`：2e18
`supplyInterestRate`=（1e16* 10e18/2e18）*（100-10）/100=4.5e16

Because 10e18>2e18, the correct calculation formula should be (1e16* 1)* (100-10)/100=9e15
Without considering `getTotalDebtValue(tokenState)`/`getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)`>1, the calculated result is 5 times larger than the correct result.
### Why should we consider this situation? 
If we do not consider the situation where getTotalDebtValue(tokenState) > getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState), the ratio may be greater than 1, so the supply rate will be amplified, causing the economic system to face the risk of instability. 
## Tools Used
Manual review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/ScaledAsset.sol#L200-L207

```sol
- uint256 supplyInterestRate = FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(
-     FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(
-         _interestRate, getTotalDebtValue(tokenState), getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState)
-     ),
-     100 - _reserveFactor,
-     100
- );

+ uint256 debtValue = getTotalDebtValue(tokenState);
+ uint256 collateralValue = getTotalCollateralValue(tokenState);
+ 
+ uint256 ratio;
+ if (debtValue > collateralValue) {
+     ratio = 1;  
+ } else {
+     ratio = FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(debtValue, 1, collateralValue);
+ }
+ 
+ uint256 intermediateValue = FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(_interestRate, ratio, 1);
+ 
+ uint256 supplyInterestRate = FixedPointMathLib.mulDivDown(
+     intermediateValue,
+     100 - _reserveFactor,
+     100
+ );

```


## Assessed type

Math

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The order of quoteToken(token0, token1) in the addPair function is reversed, resulting in incorrect order of the _storePairStatus parameters.
## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-05-predy/blob/main/src/libraries/logic/AddPairLogic.sol#L78-L87
```sol
        bool isQuoteZero = uniswapPool.token0() == stableTokenAddress;

        _storePairStatus(
            stableTokenAddress,
            _global.pairs,
            pairId,
            isQuoteZero ? uniswapPool.token1() : uniswapPool.token0(),
            isQuoteZero,
            _addPairParam
        );
```
If isQuoteZero is `true`, the quote asset is the first token in the Uniswap pool, so uniswapPool.token0() should be returned.
If isQuoteZero is `false`, the quote asset is the second token in the Uniswap pool, so uniswapPool.token1() should be returned.

In the parameters of the `_storePairStatus` function, the order of `isQuoteZero ? uniswapPool.token1() : uniswapPool.token0()` is wrong and should be reversed.

While Tether is known to do this, it applies to other tokens as well, which are trying to protect against [this attack vector](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YLPtQxZu1UAvO9cZ1O2RPXBbT0mooh4DYKjA_jp-RLM/edit)..

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Chainlink aggregators have a built-in circuit breaker if the price of an asset goes outside of a predetermined price band.The result is that if an asset experiences a huge drop in value (i.e. LUNA crash) the price of the oracle will continue to return the minPrice instead of the actual price of the asset.
 This would allow users to continue borrowing with the asset but at the wrong price. This is exactly what happened to Venus on BSC when LUNA [crashed](https://rekt.news/venus-blizz-rekt/).
